key_insight: The paper introduces interval- and fuzzy-based physics-augmented neural networks that can learn hyperelastic constitutive laws while explicitly representing uncertainty. Instead of predicting a single stress response, the models produce bounded predictions that can enclose noisy experimental data and propagate uncertainty through mechanics simulations.
problem_solved: Constitutive modeling often relies on sparse, noisy, or heterogeneous stress-deformation data, making it difficult to obtain reliable material laws and quantify uncertainty in mechanics predictions.
method: Train physics-augmented neural networks on free energy density so that stress is obtained via automatic differentiation, enforcing physical consistency.
Use interval PANNs (iPANNs) to learn lower, mean, and upper branches that bound uncertain stress responses.
Use fuzzy PANNs (fPANNs) to represent uncertainty with fuzzy membership-based outputs for more flexible uncertainty quantification and propagation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in scientific computing, this provides a principled way to build models that are both physics-informed and uncertainty-aware. It is especially useful when data are limited or noisy and confidence bounds matter for downstream simulation and decision-making.

paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
paper_authors: Somesh Pratap Singh, Govinda Anantha Padmanabha, Jingye Tan, Steven Yang, Reese E. Jones
